key_insight: An adapted machine-learning ensemble better predicted sustained antibiotic exposure in ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage across hospitals than a source-only model.
clinical_relevance: This suggests prediction models for antibiotic use in critical care may need site-specific adaptation before being trusted for decision support or benchmarking.
method: Derived ICH ICU cohorts from MIMIC-IV (source) and eICU (target).
Built multiple feature-based base models using demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, lab, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurement-density data.
Combined model outputs with clinical and data-availability features in a 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner using cross-fitting.
evidence_signal: On held-out eICU data (511 stays, 48 positives), the adapted ensemble reached AUROC 0.841 and AP 0.540, outperforming the MIMIC-IV source-only stack (AUROC 0.782).
watch_item: Performance was evaluated retrospectively and the target outcome is proxy-based and institution-dependent, so external transportability and real-world implementation still need confirmation.
paper_title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
